plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: An epiphytic cactus with segmented, flattened stems edged with pointed teeth. It produces tubular, asymmetrical flowers at the tips of its stems. It is a very popular houseplant in the Northern Hemisphere and blooms in response to short days and cool nights.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (November to January)
plants.location: Native to the coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil; widely cultivated as a houseplant worldwide
plants.funFact: In the wild it grows on trees and rocks in humid Brazilian forests, and it can live for decades, with some specimens passed down through generations of families.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, semi-deciduous tree with fern-like leaves that produces dense clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere it carpets streets and parks with purple petals as spring turns to early summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa, Australia, New Zealand and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, known as the Jacaranda City, thousands of trees bloom each spring, and in Australia a falling jacaranda blossom was once said to be a sign to start studying for exams.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and fragrant, delicate flowers that open in the cooler months. It is more sun-tolerant than other camellias and is often used for hedges, screens and espaliers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to Japan; cultivated in mild climates including the southeastern United States, the Mediterranean and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and its seeds are pressed to make a cooking and cosmetic oil in Japan.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with showy colored bracts that are often mistaken for petals; the true flowers are the small yellow clusters (cyathia) at the center. In frost-free climates it grows into a large landscape shrub that peaks around the holiday season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to Mexico; grown outdoors in tropical and subtropical regions and indoors worldwide
plants.funFact: The Aztecs called it cuetlaxochitl and used its sap to make a reddish dye and a fever medicine; it is also the subject of a long-standing myth about being poisonous, though it is only mildly irritating.
